subtype_label: Focus internal / focus inference (no given focus)
query: Help me understand what's worth analyzing in these travel-expense records.

judge.implied_focus: Travel-expense spend behavior and its anomalies/timing (amount magnitude, deviations, and processing/temporal context)

per_column.name: spend_tier
per_column.rationale: Buckets the amount into High/Medium/Low, directly framing spend magnitude as the central concept to analyze.

per_column.name: is_amount_anomaly
per_column.rationale: Flags outlier amounts, a natural analytical facet of a spend focus and directly actionable for auditing.

per_column.name: processing_days
per_column.rationale: Adds an operational/timeliness facet relevant to expense handling; loosely tied to spend but coherent as a process attribute.

per_column.name: fiscal_quarter
per_column.rationale: Temporal bucketing enabling spend trend analysis over periods; a coherent contextual facet of the spend focus.

judge.rationale: The columns cohere reasonably around spend as the inferred focus: spend_tier and is_amount_anomaly both center squarely on expense amount (magnitude and outliers), while fiscal_quarter provides a temporal axis for trend analysis. processing_days introduces a distinct operational/timeliness dimension that is useful but slightly loosens the single-focus coherence, edging toward a two-theme set (spend vs. processing efficiency). Structurally the set forms a sensible predictor/attribute mix at useful granularity — tiers, a binary anomaly flag, a numeric latency, and a period label — rather than a bare restatement or noise. The implied focus (which expenses are large/anomalous and when) is clearly investigable and actionable for audit and budgeting, so actionability is high. Minor deductions reflect the empty descriptions and the mild dilution of a single coherent focus by the processing facet.
